current_flow: MisDrillService.run (mis-drill.service.ts:27) authorizes, canonicalises the plant against scope, resolves the selection, picks the block, binds pins, reads the outline, derives the leafKey, computes leafTriples, builds queries and writes the drill audit before querying - but it is controller-oriented: it returns HTTP-shaped refusals through refuse(...) and is not exported to ChatModule. drill-transactions hard-codes LIMIT 100. classifyCausalQuestion (reconciliation-guard.ts:31) matches why/reason/explain and does NOT classify 'how is this 85000' as causal. Task 1 shipped the attested context, the grounding service and the refusal variants of the union, with nodeKey and block REQUIRED together, and a verified request returning a verified-but-unanswered outcome.
rationale: One bounded task: extract the seam once, classify intent deterministically, and answer through the drill's existing protections. It stays bounded because it adds no UI and no new query path - the sensitive query already exists and is being moved, not written. The grill's amendments widened the FILE set (the repository that owns the limit, the drill interface and controller test, the Swagger artifact) without widening the behaviour.
new_abstractions: A raw-read domain seam extracted from MisDrillService returning typed ok/replaced/gone/audit-failed outcomes with a row-limit argument. NEW because the existing service is controller-oriented and throws HTTP exceptions; without extraction this task would duplicate the sensitive pinned-batch query or lose typed outcomes to the global error filter.

A server-only verified-grounding context produced from the single authoritative batch-state read. NEW because verify() returns a public status today and the seam needs server-derived resolution, scope, pins, range and focus - rebuilding those from client fields would be a second validation path.

A statement-intent fixture table (composition | causal | data) with causal precedence. NEW because the existing guard does not classify composition wording at all, so the boundary has to be built rather than configured.

The explanation variants of the chat response union - leaf, aggregate, replaced, focus-required, safe audit-failure - extending the refusal variants task 1 shipped rather than creating a second union.
gaps: The focus wire contract made two recorded criteria IMPOSSIBLE. Task 1 shipped nodeKey and block as a REQUIRED pair, so an unfocused grounded request is rejected by the schema before the service ever runs and focus-required can never be returned; and the request carries no subject, so a crafted Budget focus is indistinguishable from an Actual one and the promised backend Budget refusal cannot exist.

The replaced answer had no shape. The contract required both a distinct replaced variant AND the leaf explanation with its transactions, without saying whether replacement is a status attached to the leaf or a complete outcome containing the leaf payload - so task 3 could not render it consistently.

The verified-read handoff was undefined. StatementGroundingService.verify() returns only a public status while the shared seam needs the server-derived resolution, scope, pins, range and focus - so an implementer would either rebuild a drill request from CLIENT fields, creating a second inconsistent validation path, or re-run every check and repeat the sensitive batch reads.

The row limit could not reach the SQL: drill-transactions hard-codes LIMIT 100 and its interface takes no limit argument, so 'the assistant asks for 20 while the panel keeps 100' would have been cosmetic - both would still have queried 100.

D-0053 could not be PROVEN from the scoped fake-only grounding test, because the real repository executes separate 'found' and 'active' SQL queries - a fake would have satisfied the leaf while the race remained in the shipped code.

The drill interface and controller test were out of scope although the contract requires the controller to map typed seam outcomes back to its shipped response - so the extraction could have silently changed the drill route's behaviour with nothing to catch it.
leafTriples() drops the mapping target, the provisional flag and the reason, so the roll-up payload could not honestly describe an unmapped-GL line as provisional - which criterion 8 requires.

The proof set omitted several recorded promises: that a grounded DATA question falls through unpinned, that the audit records the mapping-master version, and that unmapped lines are marked provisional.

Both chat routes carry DESCRIPTION-ONLY Swagger responses, so decision 0019's typed-contract requirement could have been 'satisfied' by prose while the union stayed undocumented and free to drift between the buffered and streamed routes.

The manual verification named only LLM_PROVIDER=bedrock, so a human following it would hit a startup failure or a mock provider: BEDROCK_MODEL_ID and STATEMENT_ATTESTATION_SECRETS are both required now that task 1 has shipped.
resolutions: RESOLVED: the pair becomes ONE OPTIONAL TYPED FOCUS - absent means the server returns focus-required, present means { nodeKey, block, subject: 'actual' | 'budget' }, 'budget' is a typed refusal, and only 'actual' reaches the read seam. Recorded as a criterion with leaves for both the absent-focus and crafted-budget cases.

RESOLVED by the human: replaced is ITS OWN OUTCOME carrying the full leaf explanation, transaction page and footer, plus a notice naming the source and period that went stale. A flag on an otherwise-normal answer is the kind of detail a renderer drops, and then stale figures read as current. It extends task 1's union rather than opening a parallel response channel.

RESOLVED: verification produces a SERVER-ONLY verified-grounding context from the SINGLE authoritative batch-state read, and both the chat path and the drill controller feed the seam from it. A drill request is never reconstructed from client fields. This is also the honest fix for D-0053, whose race was two separate reads.

RESOLVED: backend/src/warehouse/drill-transactions.{interface,repository}.ts and its repository test are in scope, with a leaf asserting the supplied limit reaches the query so 20 and 100 are genuinely different.
RESOLVED: the one-query repository operation is in scope and tested at the repository level, not only through a fake.
RESOLVED: backend/src/mis/mis-drill.interface.ts and mis-drill.controller.test.ts are in scope, with a leaf asserting the controller maps EVERY typed outcome to its shipped response.

RESOLVED: the typed roll-up payload carries the mapping target, provisional flag and reason, recorded as a criterion with a leaf asserting an unmapped-GL line is described as provisional with its reason.
RESOLVED: leaves added for all three, plus the absent-focus and crafted-budget cases the new focus contract makes provable.
RESOLVED: a named response DTO or schema for the union is required on both routes, with a Swagger assertion leaf in backend/src/swagger.test.ts, which is now in scope.
RESOLVED: the manual verification names all three.

rounds.question: When the pinned batch was replaced, decision 0025 says show the figures and report the replacement. But should that be its own response shape, or the normal answer with a flag on it? Task 3 renders whatever I choose here.
options: Its own outcome carrying the full explanation (Recommended)
The normal leaf answer with a status flag
rounds.chosen: Its own outcome carrying the full explanation (Recommended)

summary: Cold read of the explain-the-number contract: ten findings, and the sharpest showed task 1's own review outcome had quietly broken two of THIS task's criteria. Making nodeKey and block a required pair - the right call for task 1, where a grounded request had to carry a subject - means an unfocused request is now rejected by the schema before the service runs, so focus-required can never be returned, and with no subject field a crafted Budget focus is indistinguishable from an Actual one, so the backend Budget refusal cannot exist. The pair becomes one optional typed focus. The read also caught three things that would have made recorded promises cosmetic: drill-transactions hard-codes LIMIT 100 with no limit argument, so 20-versus-100 was unprovable; D-0053's race is in the REAL repository's two SQL queries, so a fake-only leaf would have passed while the race shipped; and leafTriples drops the provisional data needed to describe an unmapped line honestly. The human chose the replaced outcome to carry the full explanation rather than a flag a renderer could drop.
